name: Sanctions & coercion
value: France seeks EU Iran curbs; EU 22nd package due
summary: France threatened further EU sanctions on Iran on 9 Nov over a cyberattack; EU's next Russia package is expected
state: France summoned Iran's ambassador on 9 Nov and its foreign minister threatened further EU sanctions after attributing attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems to a Revolutionary Guards cyber unit (Khaleej Times). The EU added 1,646 Russia-related designations on 12 Oct, its largest single set since 2022, with a 22nd package expected next (Skadden). No major economy has been cut off from payment systems and no large seizure of sovereign assets was found as of 11 Nov.
for_you: New sanctions mainly affect firms trading with Russia or Iran and the banks and shippers that serve them. Businesses with exposure follow guidance from the UK's Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation.
rubric_hit: Major new packages and threatened EU measures on Iran: Watch line; no payment-system cut-off or sovereign asset seizure

sources.title: Khaleej Times — France accuses IRGC of cyberattack on supermarket fridges, summons Iran ambassador
Skadden — EU adopts record Russia sanctions designations as UK targets oil, crypto and supply networks

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
drivers: Russia/Iran sanctions packages, secondary sanctions, frozen-asset decisions, export controls.

rubric.alert: Major economy cut off from payment systems, or large-scale seizure of sovereign assets.
rubric.watch: Major new packages, secondary-sanction threats on large economies, or asset-seizure moves.
